review_scope: ClayCode atomic CAS semantic identity / ABA / retry identity

items.assumption: Frank/UnifiedDB/Harness need stable versioned semantic identity across concurrent state transitions.
items.independent_discriminator: Rust official compare_exchange ABA warning plus deterministic 200000-case ABA executable discriminator
items.result: The stronger mechanism-level statement is narrower: value equality is insufficient identity when the state contract allows A->B->A; version/epoch binding or an equivalent anti-ABA mechanism is required for that class.

items.assumption: Replay requires deterministic treatment of atomic concurrency.
items.independent_discriminator: weak-CAS retry identity fuzz plus C11 and ECMAScript concurrent CAS execution
items.result: Stable semantic op/outcome identity can coexist with backend- and contention-dependent physical retry traces; retry count is not default semantic state.

adversarial_checks.counterhypothesis: Atomicity alone prevents stale state transitions.
adversarial_checks.detail: A->B->A restores the compared value and lets a stale value-only CAS succeed.

adversarial_checks.counterhypothesis: Every weak-CAS physical attempt must enter semantic hash identity.
adversarial_checks.detail: The same intended semantic operation retained one semantic hash across 16 valid retry-count variants; real C11 and Node runs reached identical exact totals with differing retry counts.

adversarial_checks.counterhypothesis: SeqCst-only should be promoted as permanent ClayCode law now.
adversarial_checks.detail: SeqCst is retained only as an OPEN BASE-portable default candidate. No multi-architecture production benchmark yet justifies forbidding weaker explicit orderings permanently.

authority_boundary: Frank remains a separate research subject; this review creates no Frank self-Harness authority.
